title: RobCo raises Series C funding to scale industrial automation - The Robot Report
content:
![三个机械臂。RobCo 将物理人工智能和模块化硬件应用于工业自动化。](https://www.therobotreport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/RobCo_Lightspeed-copy.jpg)
RobCo 将物理人工智能和模块化硬件应用于工业自动化。来源：Lightspeed Venture Partners

新年伊始，机器人领域迎来了新的资金注入。RobCo GmbH 今天表示，已筹集了 1 亿美元的 C 轮融资，以推进其物理人工智能路线图，扩大企业部署，并深化其在美国市场的业务。

“凭借额外的 1 亿美元资金，我们将成为美国和欧洲制造业领域占据主导地位的人工智能机器人公司，”RobCo 创始人兼首席执行官 Roman Hölzl 表示。“这将使我们能够实现自动化普通任务的目标，从而让人类能够从事非凡的工作。”

RobCo 成立于 2020 年，表示其开发的机器人系统将学习和自主性引入[工业](https://www.therobotreport.com/category/robots-platforms/industrial-robots/)运营。这家总部位于慕尼黑的[公司](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/robco/)表示，其自主制造平台将模块化硬件与物理[人工智能](https://www.therobotreport.com/category/design-development/ai-cognition/)软件堆栈相结合，从而实现快速部署、持续改进和特定于应用程序的性能。

## RobCo 构建用于自主性的全栈平台

RobCo 声称，它“从第一天起就实现了垂直整合，将硬件和软件开发为一个完整的全栈平台”。该平台结合了感知、[运动](https://www.therobotreport.com/category/robot-components/motioncontrol/)规划和自学习方法，从而在实际生产环境中实现日益自主的机器人操作。

该公司表示，其机器人可以通过演示和自学习来获得特定于任务的技能，而不是手动编程。这可以实现快速部署和迭代，以及更容易地适应复杂或可变的过程。RobCo 声称，它充当客户的“单一窗口”。

此外，RobCo 表示，它设计的系统“旨在减少当今流程与端到端自动化之间的摩擦，使团队能够减少设置和维护系统的时间，而将更多精力放在其核心业务流程和价值驱动因素上。”

![使用人工智能的机械臂。RobCo 已扩展到美国制造业。](https://www.therobotreport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/RobCo_banner.jpg)
RobCo 已扩展到美国制造业。来源：RobCo

## 为美国企业扩展部署

RobCo 通过重复性的机器人即服务 ([RaaS](https://www.automatedwarehouseonline.com/category/raas/)) 模式提供其技术，该公司表示，这有助于公司自动化手动任务，同时最大限度地降低运营复杂性和风险。该公司支持广泛的工作流程，包括[机器管理](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/machine-tending)、[托盘堆垛](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/palletizing/)、分配和[焊接](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/welding/)。

去年，RobCo 扩展到美国，目前在旧金山和奥斯汀设有办事处。该公司指出，由于[制造商](https://www.therobotreport.com/category/markets-industries/manufacturing/)加快了自动化工作以应对劳动力限制、[回流](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/reshoring)计划和运营复杂性的上升，美国已成为战略重点和主要增长市场。

RobCo 补充说，其机器人已部署在各种工业环境中，从宝马等大型全球制造商到 DynaEnergetics、Fabricated Extrusion Company、T-Systems 和 Rosenberger 等公司。

## Lightspeed 加倍投资工业机器人

Lightspeed Venture Partners 和 Lingotto Innovation 领投了 RobCo 的 C 轮融资。其他参与者包括 Sequoia Capital、Greenfield Partners、Kindred Capital、Leitmotif 和 The Friedkin Group。

Lightspeed 的合伙人 Alexander Schmitt 表示：“在领投 RobCo 的 [B 轮融资](https://www.therobotreport.com/robco-raises-42-5m-for-automation-for-small-midsize-manufacturers/)之后，我们很高兴加倍投资并共同领投这轮 1 亿美元的融资。”“我们的标准非常高，RobCo 不断提高现代机器人在现实生产中的标准。”

他补充说：“RobCo 拥有打造全球冠军所需的一切：今天已经在工业环境中交付的系统，以及基于物理人工智能的平台，该平台可以跨用例和地域扩展。”

RobCo 表示，其风险投资投资者拥有构建定义类别技术公司的经验，而其工业投资者则利用行业内的深厚联系来长期支持成长型公司。

Exor 旗下的投资管理公司 Lingotto Innovation 的管理合伙人兼联席主管 Morgan Samet 表示：“制造业正在进入一个新阶段，自主性将成为决定性的优势。”“RobCo 的突出之处在于它将物理人工智能引入实际生产环境，将今天经过验证的部署与迈向更高自主性的清晰、循序渐进的路径相结合——允许学习系统在工厂车间最重要的地方为人们提供支持。”

![Three robotic arms. RobCo applies physical AI and modular hardware to industrial automation.](https://www.therobotreport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/RobCo_Lightspeed-copy.jpg)
RobCo applies physical AI and modular hardware to industrial automation. Source: Lightspeed Venture Partners
The new year is bringing fresh funding across the robotics landscape. RobCo GmbH today said it has raised Series C funding of $100 million to advance its physical AI roadmap, expand enterprise deployments, and deepen its presence in the U.S. market.
“With $100 million of additional funding, we will become the dominant AI robotics company for manufacturing in the U.S. and Europe,” stated Roman Hölzl, founder and CEO of RobCo. “This will allow us to execute on our purpose of automating the ordinary, so humans can do the extraordinary.”
Founded in 2020, RobCo said it develops robotic systems that bring learning and autonomy into [industrial](https://www.therobotreport.com/category/robots-platforms/industrial-robots/) operations. The Munich-based [company](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/robco/) said its Autonomous Manufacturing Platform combines modular hardware with a physical [AI](https://www.therobotreport.com/category/design-development/ai-cognition/) software stack that enables fast deployment, continuous improvement, and application-specific performance.
## RobCo builds full-stack platform for autonomy
RobCo asserted that it “has been vertically integrated from Day 1, developing hardware and software as a single full-stack platform.” The platform combines perception, [motion](https://www.therobotreport.com/category/robot-components/motioncontrol/) planning, and self-learning methods to enable increasingly autonomous robot operations inside real production environments.
The company said its robots can acquire task-specific skills through demonstration and self-learning rather than manual programming. This allows for rapid deployment and iteration, as well as easier adaptation to complex or variable processes. RobCo claimed that it acts as a “single pane of glass” for customers.
In addition, RobCo said it designed its system “to reduce friction between today’s processes and end-to-end automation, allowing teams to focus less on setting up and maintaining systems and more on their core business processes and value drivers.”
![Robotic arm using AI. RobCo has expanded into U.S. manufacturing.](https://www.therobotreport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/RobCo_banner.jpg)
RobCo has expanded into U.S. manufacturing. Source: RobCo
## Deployments scale for U.S. enterprises
RobCo delivers its technology through a recurring robotics-as-a-service ( [RaaS](https://www.automatedwarehouseonline.com/category/raas/)) model, which it said helps companies automate manual tasks while minimizing operational complexity and risk. The company supports a wide range of workflows, including [machine tending](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/machine-tending), [palletizing](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/palletizing/), dispensing, and [welding](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/welding).
Last year, RobCo expanded into the U.S., and it now operates in San Francisco and Austin. The U.S. has become both a strategic priority and a major growth market as [manufacturers](https://www.therobotreport.com/category/markets-industries/manufacturing/) accelerate automation efforts in response to labor constraints, [reshoring](https://www.therobotreport.com/tag/reshoring) initiatives, and rising operational complexity, the company noted.
RobCo added that its robots are deployed across a range of industrial environments, from large global manufacturers such as BMW to companies including DynaEnergetics, Fabricated Extrusion Company, T-Systems, and Rosenberger.
## Lightspeed doubles down on industrial robotics
Lightspeed Venture Partners and Lingotto Innovation led RobCo’s Series C round. Other participants included Sequoia Capital, Greenfield Partners, Kindred Capital, Leitmotif, and The Friedkin Group.
“After leading RobCo’s [Series B](https://www.therobotreport.com/robco-raises-42-5m-for-automation-for-small-midsize-manufacturers/), we’re excited to double down and co-lead this $100 million round,” said Alexander Schmitt, a partner at Lightspeed. “Our bar is exceptionally high, and RobCo has continued to raise the standard for what modern robotics can look like in real-world production.”
“RobCo has what it takes to build a global champion: systems that already deliver in industrial environments today and a platform grounded in physical AI that can scale across use cases and geographies,” he added.
RobCo said its venture capital investors have experience building category-defining technology companies, while its industrial investors use deep connections in industry to back growth companies over the long term.
“Manufacturing is entering a new phase where autonomy will be a decisive advantage,” said Morgan Samet, managing partner and co-head of Lingotto Innovation, an investment management company now owned by Exor. “RobCo stands out because it brings physical AI into real production environments, combining proven deployment today with a clear, step-by-step path toward higher autonomy — allowing learning systems to support people where it matters most on the factory floor.”
